walkthrough:
Prove perpendicularity before using the side lengths as base and height.
Calculate the gradients of segments $PQ$ and $QR$:
$$m_{PQ} = \dfrac{5 - 2}{5 - 1} = \dfrac{3}{4}$$
$$m_{QR} = \dfrac{9 - 5}{2 - 5} = \dfrac{4}{-3} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$$

Multiply the two gradients:
$$m_{PQ} \times m_{QR} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right) = -1$$
Since $m_{PQ} \times m_{QR} = -1$, the line segments $PQ$ and $QR$ are perpendicular, hence triangle $PQR$ is right-angled at $Q$.

hints: Since the triangle is right-angled at $Q$, $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PQ \times QR$.
walkthrough:
Prove perpendicularity before using the side lengths as base and height.
Calculate the lengths of the two legs $PQ$ and $QR$:
$$PQ = \sqrt{(5 - 1)^2 + (5 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5$$
$$QR = \sqrt{(2 - 5)^2 + (9 - 5)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PQ \times QR = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 5 = 12.5$$
